They in turn acknowledge this in Jr 42:6 , "the Lord our God." few of many-- as had been foretold ( Le 26:22 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10502"/><div sID="gen18727" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10502"/><hi type="bold">7. ten days--</hi>Jeremiah did not speak of himself, but waited God's time and revelation, showing the reality of his inspiration. Man left to himself would have given an immediate response to the people, who were impatient of delay. The delay was designed to test the sincerity of their professed willingness to obey, and that they should have full time to deliberate (<reference osisRef="Deut.8.2">De 8:2</reference>). True obedience bows to God's time, as well as His way and will. <div eID="gen18727" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv10508"/><div sID="gen18736" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv10508"/><hi type="bold">16. sword, which ye feared, shall overtake you--</hi>The very evils we think to escape by sin, we bring on ourselves thereby. What our hearts are most set on often proves fatal to us. Those who think to escape troubles by changing their place will find them wherever they go (<reference osisRef="Ezek.11.8">Eze 11:8</reference>). The "sword" here is that of Nebuchadnezzar, who fulfilled the prediction in his expedition to Africa (according to Megasthenes, a heathen writer), 300 B.C. <div eID="gen18736" type="x-p"/>
